newsitem.title: GERMANY: German official sees Airbus as stock company by 99.
newsitem.headline: German official sees Airbus as stock company by 99.

text.p: Europe's aircraft maker Airbus Industrie is expected to be be turned into a stock company under French law within two years, a senior official at its German partner Daimler-Benz Aerospace Airbus said at the weekend.

Gustav Humbert, who heads the managment at the German Airbus partner, told German newspaper Sueddeutsche Zeitung that the move, planned to ready Airbus for greater competition, is planned to occur before 1999.

A day earlier Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa) said it had no comment on a report in this week's news magazine Der Spiegel that partners in the four-nation Airbus Industrie would agree a restructuring in January.
"Dasa cannot and will not make any comment before the consortium's restructuring talks are completed," a spokesman said in response to an enquiry.
The spokesman added that Dasa favours restructuring the Airbus group into a limited liability company.
Spiegel said that a compromise restructuring plan would be signed at a supervisory board meeting on January 3 to turn Airbus into a joint-stock company under French law.
The move aims to better position Airbus to compete against Boeing and McDonnell-Douglas, which are merging.

Under the plan, France's Aerospatiale, British Aerospace, Dasa and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas would bring part of their production facilities as assets into the new company, Spiegel said, quoting unnamed sources.
Dasa would contribute two or three of its five Airbus plants.
The partners' plants would be valued by March 1997, by when a new management structure would also be agreed, Spiegel said.

The plan represents a compromise between Anglo-German efforts to bring in as many assets as possible into the new Airbus structure, and fears at Aerospatiale that it would be weakened if it gave up too much of its operating facilities.
Dasa is a unit of auto giant Daimler-Benz AG.
